trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going down-left would force the line onto number 3 before its turn; going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going up-right would strand number 3: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
I can't rule out left or up-left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Going up-left leaves no safe move afterwards; going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up-right.
Going up-left leaves no safe move afterwards; going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up-right.
Going up-right would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Going up-left would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down-left.
Cell (-3,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.
Going up-right, the next 7 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 11. So the line goes up-left.

Going up-left would strand number 9: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going left would turn number 9 into a dead-end pocket with no way out (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.
Going to number 11 leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up-right.
Number 11 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up-right would cut off the right side (5 cells); going right would cut off the right side (4 cells). So the line goes up-left.

Going up-left would leave both number 19 and cell (3,-3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up-right would cut off the top-right corner (5 cells) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-left.
Number 17 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up-right would turn number 19 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes up-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going down-right would turn number 21 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
